_comment: Decade Trivia topic taxonomy. presetTopics ids must match TOPIC_OPTIONS in frontend/src/utils/studio/decade-trivia/config.ts. aliases map the human labels a model tends to return back onto those ids. topicGuidance tells the writer what a printable question for each topic looks like — the filters downstream are strict, so a topic the model writes badly is a topic that ends up missing from the page. topicCues are raw regex fragments (NOT escaped) that decide which topic a question is really about: a question is rejected when its text belongs to a topic the author did not tick. Every preset needs both guidance and cues — a gap in either table is a gap in the promise that a ticked topic appears and an unticked one does not. The verification pass assigns the final topic; these cues are a fast pre-filter, not the last word.

presetTopics.tv: TV (television shows, hosts, series — not movies)
presetTopics.products: Products & brands (household brands, ads, gadgets, cars)
presetTopics.food: Food (meals, snacks, drinks, restaurants of the era)
presetTopics.toys: Toys & games (toys, board games, playground crazes)
presetTopics.everyday: Everyday life (household routines, shopping, mail, fashion habits, daily chores — not TV, movies, or concerts)
presetTopics.events: Events (widely remembered public moments of the decade)

topicGuidance.music: Name the act, the song title, the dance craze or the record format ("which group recorded ...", "which dance swept the ..."). Never quote a lyric, and do not ask for chart positions.
topicGuidance.tv: Name the series, the character, the host or the kind of show ("which sitcom featured ...", "which family hosted ..."). Never quote dialogue or a catchphrase.
topicGuidance.film: Name the film, the star or the role ("which musical starred ...", "which actress played ..."). Never quote a line of dialogue.
topicGuidance.products: This topic is about things people bought and used: which company made a product, what a popular car, appliance, camera or gadget was called, what a household brand was known for, or how people shopped (mail-order catalogues, department stores, trading stamps). State brand and model names as plain facts — that is the whole point of the topic — but never build a question out of a slogan, jingle, advertising line or logo wording, and stay away from tobacco and alcohol brands.
topicGuidance.food: Name the dish, snack, drink, cereal or restaurant chain, or how food was packaged and served ("which frozen meal ...", "which chain opened ...").
topicGuidance.toys: Name the toy, doll, board game or playground craze, or who made it.
topicGuidance.everyday: Home and daily routines: chores, wash day, the milkman, the telephone, shopping trips, school days, hairstyles and clothing habits. Not TV, films or concerts.
topicGuidance.events: Widely remembered public moments: space flights, world's fairs, coronations, the Olympics and other championships, first flights. Keep them warm and celebratory — no disasters, crimes or politics.
